item.title: Jazz in the Plaza — Sun Oct 18, 1:00 PM — Putnam Plaza
item.description:
Every Sunday: Free, live jazz every week performed by some of the best musicians in the SF Bay Area and beyond, right in the heart of downtown Petaluma! Every Sunday from 1 to 3:30, local jazz bassist and music book publisher Chuck Sher presents a rotating ensemble of professional, veteran jazz musicians in Putnam Plaza Park, right next to the Speakeasy. This event started in 2020 and has since become a staple for locals and visitors alike. Stop by and enjoy some of the best jazz the Bay Area has to offer!
Source: GoLocal Cooperative

item.title: Baby Bounce — Tue Oct 20, 9:30 AM — Vallejo John F. Kennedy Library
item.description:
Just for babies and their grownups! Bring your baby for some cozy, active time on your lap. Baby storytime is designed for meaningful one-on-one interaction between baby and caregiver. We'll have songs, rhymes, a book or two, and plenty of activities for both of you that are developmentally appropriate for children from birth to when they start walking. Storytime is followed by some time to stay and play with your baby or talk to other caregivers. This storytime is geared toward ages 0-2.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Healdsburg Senior Center Book Club — Tue Oct 20, 10:00 AM — Healdsburg Senior Center
item.description:
Join us on the Third Tuesday of the month at 10:00 am as we discuss different books! Print Copies will be available in the branch a month before the discussion. Please call or email the library with any questions. Book Club titles and dates are subject to change. For up to date information visit: sonomalibrary.org/bookclubs 2026 Schedule January 20 - North Woods by Daniel Mason February 17 - The Housemaid by Freida McFadden March 17 - Three Bags Full by Leonie Swann April 21 - Maid by Stephanie Land May 19 - Good Night Irene by Luis Alberto Urrea June 16 - Nightshade by Michael Connelly July 21 - Daisy Darker by Alice Feeney August 18 - My Friends by Fredrick Backman September 15 - The Truth According to Ember by Danica Nava October 20 - A Marriage at Sea by Sophie Elmhirst November 17 - Anita de Monte Laughs Last by Xociti Gonzalez December 15 - TBD
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Movies 'n Munchies — Wed Oct 21, 5:00 PM — Vallejo John F. Kennedy Library
item.description:
Frankenweenie, a Tim Burton film, is the heartwarming tale about a boy, Victor, who uses science to bring his beloved dog Sparky back to life. As Victor delves into regeneration experiments, he and his town come to learn of the unexpected, monstrous consequences of his science experiment. During the film, thematic snacks will be served to enhance the experience! Registration is required. Please note: Participants must be 13 years of age or older.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Lawyers in the Library — Wed Oct 21, 5:30 PM — Vallejo John F. Kennedy Library
item.description:
The Vallejo JFK Library offers the Lawyers in the Library programon the first and third Wednesdays of every month. Each meeting is 15 minutes. Space is limited and slots fill up on a first come, first serve basis. Please callor come in-person to Vallejo JFK Library at 9am on the day of the program to reserve a spot. Currently, our program offers phone consultations with a lawyer. If you have an appointment, the attorney will call you that evening between 5:30 - 7:15pm. PLEASE NOTE: In-person meetings are not currently offered. Coming to the library during the scheduled appointment window will not result in an in-person meeting. You will need a working phone to receive the call. The library is unable to provide telephone access for a lawyer consultation. If you would like more information, please call us at \(866\) 572-7587.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Saturday Harvest Market at Sonoma Garden Park — Sat Oct 24, 9:00 AM — Sonoma Garden Park
item.description:
Saturday Harvest Markets are back! 2026 Harvest Markets reopen March 21 and continue until December. Harvest Markets take place every Saturday, 9:00 am-1:00 pm. The Harvest Market is a great place to pick up organic produce, fresh flowers, and vegetable starts from our 6.1 acre sustainable garden! We also sell locally sourced olive oil, honey, and farm fresh eggs from our Sonoma neighbors. The market accepts credit cards and Apple Pay. Remember to bring your reusable shopping bag! Photo by Melania Mahoney
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Hallowine Walk — Sat Oct 24, 12:00 PM — Town of Yountville
item.description:
HALLOWINE WALK
Trick, Treat, & Taste in Yountville
Saturday, October 24, 2026 12:00 – 4:00 p.m. Washington St. | Yountville
Celebrate Halloween with a spirited afternoon in the heart of Yountville!
Join us for the inaugural Hallowine Walk: Trick, Treat & Taste in Yountville, where wine, Halloween, and small-town charm come together for a one-of-a-kind fall experience.
Your ticket includes a commemorative wine cup, event wristband, and tasting map. After checking in at Veterans Memorial Park, you’ll stroll through Yountville, visiting participating wineries, tasting rooms, restaurants, and local businesses while enjoying wine tastings, festive décor, seasonal surprises, and exclusive event-day offerings.
Costumes are encouraged, so gather your friends, dress in your Halloween best, and enjoy an unforgettable afternoon of wine, treats, and festive fun!
Ticket Includes:
Hallowine Walk cup
Wine tastings at participating locations
Event wristband and tasting map
Access to exclus

item.title: Every Which Way but Up — Sat Oct 24, 4:00 PM — Hammerfriar Gallery & Custom Framing
item.description:
New Work by, Todd Barricklow & Art Moura
Opening: Oct 24, 4-6pm
Through January, 2027
**Todd Barricklow** inspired by the classical amphora as a vessel of culture and utility, his work continues this tradition by depicting, in narrative tension, the tools, machinery, and transportation of our place in time.
**Art Moura** is a painter and sculptor working with paper, wood and found materials. Through imagery that is at once tender, sometimes brutal, and emotionally raw, his work embraces the inescapably ephemeral and poignant truths of life.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat
